clue.text: Punch Frank but not 'ard

indicators.note: but not tells us to take the following letters away from the footballer's surname

parts.note: Frank Lampard, the England and Chelsea footballer
the letters as written, the dropped-aitch spelling of hard

explanation.surface: An instruction to hit someone named Frank, but gently, in a Cockney accent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like an adjective or a name to hit; it stands for the footballer Frank Lampard, and 'but not' removes the ARD.
explanation.definitionFit: To lamp someone is British slang for hitting them, a straight synonym for the verb punch.

clue.text: Fancy dishes ruin empty gastropubs

parts.note: to do in someone or something is to wreck or destroy it

indicators.note: empty means the inside of gastropubs is cleared, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A grumble that elaborate cooking spoils gastropubs and leaves them deserted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like an anagram signal; it belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers gives the plural colloquial noun as elaborate dishes or a feast, alongside its sense of things and activities.

clue.text: Liberal laughing about politician could be awkward

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the politician
liberal means free with things, so the letters of laughing are freely rearranged

parts.note: MP, Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A Liberal Democrat chortling about a fellow politician might make for an awkward moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal' looks like the party; it is the anagram signal on 'laughing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving in a clumsy, heavy, lumbering way is being awkward; the word is Lewis Carroll's coinage.

clue.text: In retirement hopeless case gets hot on Eastern religion

indicators.note: something in retirement goes back, so the selected letters are read backwards
the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

parts.note: keen on something, informally into it

explanation.surface: A retired no-hoper takes up a fervent interest in an Eastern faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hopeless case' looks like a phrase for a loser; 'case' takes the outer letters H and S of 'hopeless', and 'In retirement' turns them to SH.
explanation.definitionFit: Japan's native faith, centred on nature spirits and ancestor worship, is an Eastern religion.

clue.text: Parents accepting girl's perspective

indicators.note: accepting means the parents take the girl inside them

parts.note: pa and ma, father and mother
Nora, a girl's name

explanation.surface: A mother and father take on board their daughter's point of view.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide unbroken view of an area, or a broad survey of a subject, is a perspective on it.

clue.text: Is it muddy intermittently? It's a farm!

indicators.note: intermittently means taking every other letter of the words is it muddy, starting with the second

explanation.surface: A visitor asks if a place is muddy and is told that, being a farm, of course it is.
explanation.definitionFit: A place where horses are kept for breeding is a farm of that kind.

clue.text: Note old crock coming after stylish Elan in producing improved air-fuel ratio

indicators.note: the note and crock are placed after the rearranged letters
stylish suggests the letters of Elan are given a new style, a rearrangement

parts.note: B, a musical note
a crock is an earthenware pot, and an ancient one is an urn

explanation.surface: A tune-up on a classic Lotus Elan gives an old banger a better fuel mixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old crock' looks like a worn-out car beside the Elan sports car; here it is a pot.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine of this kind runs on a mixture with a high proportion of air, saving fuel, so it improves the air-fuel ratio.

clue.text: Secret trend spread with no new popular acceptance

indicators.note: spread means the letters are scattered and rearranged
with no means the letter for new is removed from trend

parts.note: N, the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A hidden fashion spreading without anything new in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Credibility among ordinary young people, the standing that comes from being in touch with fashion, is a kind of popular acceptance.

clue.text: Welcome look adopted by Scandinavian rockers

indicators.note: adopted by means the look is taken in by the band

parts.note: A-ha, the Norwegian pop group
lo, an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: A Norwegian band adopts a welcoming look.
explanation.walkthrough: A-ha were the Norwegian band behind 'Take On Me'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hawaiian greeting is used both for hello and goodbye, so it serves as a welcome.

clue.text: Listen to the Four Tops let loose — that's soulful

parts.note: to hear something is to listen to it

indicators.note: tops means the first letters of the words the and four
let loose means the letters of let are set free and rearranged

explanation.surface: An invitation to listen to Motown's Four Tops singing freely, which is real soul music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Four Tops' reads as the Motown group, but 'Tops' takes T and F from 'the Four'.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling that comes from the heart is deep and sincere, which is what soulful describes.

clue.text: What's black and white? The Swan's half of stout

parts.note: a pen is a female swan

indicators.note: half of means only the first half of the brand of stout is kept

parts.note: Guinness, the famous Irish stout

explanation.surface: A riddle about black and white things, set in a pub called the Swan where someone orders a half of stout.
explanation.walkthrough: The Swan reads as a pub, and 'half of stout' as a drink order; a stout is black with a white head.
explanation.definitionFit: The flightless Antarctic bird with its dark back and pale front is the classic black-and-white thing in riddles.

clue.text: New father with daughter protected by men in the outskirts of Eastbourne

parts.note: OR, other ranks, the ordinary soldiers, who stand beside the daughter as guards
D, the abbreviation for daughter

indicators.note: the outskirts of a word are its outer letters, the first and last

explanation.surface: A recent dad and his daughter guarded by soldiers on the edge of the seaside town of Eastbourne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New father' is not a recent dad but a newly ordained priest, a Father.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone just admitted to holy orders is a newly made priest, addressed as Father.

clue.text: Legendary pea soup served up elsewhere

indicators.note: served suggests the pea soup letters are dished out in a new order
elsewhere means the word up goes somewhere else, taken out of the letters of pea soup

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A legendary bowl of pea soup is served somewhere else.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of 'pea soup' are rearranged with those of 'up' removed. 'Legendary' stands for the fabled Greek storyteller, himself perhaps a legend.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek teller of animal fables may never have existed, so he is a semi-legendary figure.

clue.text: Assorted pies and pates about right for hors d'oeuvres

indicators.note: about means the mixed letters go around the abbreviation for right
assorted means the letters of pies and pates are mixed together

parts.note: R, the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A selection of pies and pâtés seems just right to serve as starters.
explanation.definitionFit: Small savoury dishes served before a meal to stimulate the appetite are hors d'oeuvres.

clue.text: Coconut whirls, seen around North America as a part payment

indicators.note: seen around means the spun letters sit around the abbreviation
whirls means the letters of coconut are spun round into a new order

parts.note: NA, the abbreviation for North America

explanation.surface: Coconut sweets are spotted all over North America, bought in instalments.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying on account means paying part of what is owed, an idiom for an interim payment.

clue.text: Conservative interest level is assuming key debt may be unpredictable

parts.note: C, the abbreviation for Conservative
APR, annual percentage rate

indicators.note: assuming means taking on, so the word is takes in the key and the debt

parts.note: taken as written
C, a musical key
IOU, a written acknowledgement of a debt

explanation.surface: A Tory remark that an interest rate which takes on major debt could be volatile.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone or something given to sudden changes of mood or behaviour is fickle and hard to predict.

clue.text: Real chips cooked in pasta recipe? That makes a point

indicators.note: in means the cooked letters go inside the pasta

parts.note: penne, tube-shaped pasta

indicators.note: cooked means the letters of real chips are worked into a new arrangement

parts.note: R, the abbreviation for recipe, from the Latin on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A cook wonders whether real chips are going into a pasta recipe, and is told that it proves a point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That makes a point' reads as someone winning an argument; the device literally gives a pencil its point.
explanation.definitionFit: The little bladed tool sharpens a pencil to a tip, so it literally makes a point.

clue.text: Pest is in touch

indicators.note: in means the word is goes inside the word for touch

parts.note: a slight touch or shade of difference is a nuance

explanation.surface: A pest is one who keeps in touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone or something annoying is a pest, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Where Saint Omer's situated?

parts.note: S, an abbreviation for saint
taken as written
something set somewhere is situated there

explanation.surface: A question asking where the French town of Saint-Omer is to be found.
explanation.walkthrough: Saint-Omer is in northern France, not this English county; the question mark admits it, since only the letters S and OMER are situated in the county.
explanation.definitionFit: The English county in the south-west is the place where S and OMER are placed, given SET round them in the reading.

clue.text: Emaciated toothless person whose name I can't recall

definitions.text: person whose name I can't recall

parts.note: emaciated means very thin
without teeth, one shows only gums

explanation.surface: Describing a gaunt, toothless old man whose name escapes the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one description of a forgotten person; split 4,5, the answer is that person too.
explanation.definitionFit: A placeholder word used for someone or something whose name has been forgotten, like whatsit or whatsisname.

clue.text: Sycophant longing to cover up majority of smarm

indicators.note: to cover up means the word for longing goes around the other piece

parts.note: a yen is a longing

indicators.note: majority of means the larger part of the word smarm is kept, losing its last two letters

explanation.surface: A toady who longs to hide most of his oily charm.
explanation.definitionFit: A sycophant agrees with everything a superior says, the classic flatterer and toady.

clue.text: United out of sorts?

definitions.meaning: commercial slang for two companies joined in a partnership, together as if sharing a bed
someone unwell might be lying under the covers

explanation.surface: Manchester United are playing below their best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United' reads as the football club; it is a verb meaning joined.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharing a bed implies being joined together, and an ailing person stays tucked up there, so both senses fit.

clue.text: Working close to home in bar coming back with mug

indicators.note: in means the two pieces go inside the reversed bar
coming back means the word for bar is read in reverse

parts.note: a pub is a bar
on means operating, working

indicators.note: close to means the final letter of the word home

explanation.surface: Someone working near home in a bar comes back carrying a beer mug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mug' looks like a beer glass in the bar picture; it is the verb, as in mug up.
explanation.definitionFit: To mug up is British slang for cramming study, the same as revising a subject hard.

clue.text: Bolt's quicker with change of temperature

indicators.note: change of temperature means hot is swapped for cold, H for C

parts.note: sharper means quicker, as of wit

explanation.surface: Usain Bolt is faster when the weather changes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bolt' looks like the sprinter; it is the verb meaning flee. H and C are the abbreviations for hot and cold.
explanation.definitionFit: To run away quickly is to bolt, and the British slang verb means to flee.

clue.text: Individual involved in bondage, open to change

indicators.note: open to change means the letters of open are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone into bondage who is open-minded about new things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bondage' suggests something kinky; it means servitude.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin American labourer held in debt servitude to a landowner is a person in bondage.

clue.text: Ukip's right wing stopping crook becoming political strategist

indicators.note: stopping means the letter plugs the middle of the word for crook

parts.note: a wrongdoer, a sinner

indicators.note: the right wing of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: UKIP's right-wingers block a villain from becoming a party spin doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: UKIP is a British right-wing party; 'right wing' just means the last letter of 'Ukip'.
explanation.definitionFit: A spin doctor who presents events favourably for a party is a political strategist.

clue.text: European mountain dweller's heart and character

indicators.note: heart means only the central letters of the word for the mountain dweller are kept

parts.note: a Tyrolean lives in the Tyrol, in the Alps

explanation.surface: Praise for the heart and character of a man from the Alps.
explanation.definitionFit: A part played by an actor is a character in a play.

clue.text: Who developed this form runs rings round half of pack given pressure and time

parts.note: R, the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: round means the rings sit around the other piece

parts.note: two rings look like two letter Os

indicators.note: half of means the back half of the word pack is kept

parts.note: P, the abbreviation for pressure
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A puzzle over who invented a format, involving running rings round half a pack under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Who' looks like a question word; it is The Who, the band whose 'Tommy' pioneered the form.
explanation.definitionFit: The Who's Tommy was a landmark album telling a story in songs, the genre they helped develop.

clue.text: Typical finding sheep and Surrey town in the news

indicators.note: being in the news means being spoken about on air, so the words are said out loud

parts.note: a ewe is a female sheep, and Ewell is a town in Surrey

explanation.surface: A typical local news story about sheep in a Surrey town.
explanation.walkthrough: Ewell is a town in Surrey, south-west of London; said quickly, ewe plus Ewell approximates the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Normal or customary is what typical means, a straightforward synonym.
